_comment: Chrome/Chromium launch flags for showtime capture. Read by scripts/lib/chrome.mjs and lib/st/platform.py. 'common' always applies; 'gpu' is per OS for the hardware path; 'software' replaces it when GPU is off. 'render' is added for showtime render only, per OS like 'gpu' (a plain list applies on every OS). --disable-frame-rate-limit draws a frame when asked, not on the next 60 Hz tick: 0-9 % faster renders in the 0.4.1 measurements, about 10 % against the same code without it for a 20 s 1080p DOM page with SwiftShader on an 8-thread Linux machine (2026-10-09). It is on Linux only. With it a renderer keeps spending CPU after the GPU process stops, so on macOS the stuck-frame guard (stagehost.mjs guardShot) never sees a stopped GPU process: on an Intel Mac with a GPU the stall test fails with it and passes without, and it bought about 2 % (inside run-to-run spread) for about 22 % more CPU while rendering (2026-10-09). It is the likely cause of the stalls of renders and the tests around them on the 3-thread macOS CI runners in 0.4.1 (where an idle render page was seen drawing back to back at about 0.4 of a core; not reproduced since: about 0.015 of a core either way on Linux, under 1 % for a static page on that Mac; not measured inside the render harness). Windows is untested with the guard and stays without it, as before 0.4.1. On Linux the guard still ends a frame that never comes with the flag on (test_pace.py TestFrameNeverComes). Not for live playback either (it broke the HTML video's audio start in the export tests).
